skills.name: auto-complete
skills.summary: Turn rough notes, pseudocode, or broken code into a working program.
skills.example: Use $auto-complete to implement this pseudocode in Python and explain the result.

skills.name: brainstorming-agent
skills.summary: Talk through an idea, compare your options, and decide what to try next.
skills.example: Use $brainstorming-agent to help me compare two approaches to my side project.

skills.name: code-concept-map
skills.summary: See which programming concepts a project uses in an interactive map.
skills.example: Use $code-concept-map to map the engineering concepts in this repository.

skills.name: code-execution-path
skills.summary: Follow a request or action through the code, step by step.
skills.example: Use $code-execution-path to trace what happens when a user submits this form.

skills.name: idea-council-agent
skills.summary: Test a project idea from four angles: purpose, demand, cost, and how to build it.
skills.example: Use $idea-council-agent to evaluate this project idea before I build it.

skills.name: interviewer-agent
skills.summary: Practise an interview for your role or project and get feedback on your answers.
skills.example: Use $interviewer-agent for a backend engineering interview based on this project.

skills.name: language-tutor
skills.summary: Learn to speak a language through guided lessons, conversation, and review.
skills.example: Use $language-tutor to plan a beginner spoken Spanish course.

skills.name: personal-context
skills.summary: Keep your goals and preferences available across sessions, with changes you approve.
skills.example: Use $personal-context to show the keys in my approved profile.

skills.name: reading-agent
skills.summary: Read a book or PDF together, discuss each part, and save where you stopped.
skills.example: Use $reading-agent to read this PDF with me, one chapter at a time.

skills.name: self-help-agent
skills.summary: Talk through difficult feelings or recurring frustrations and explore ways to cope.
skills.example: Use $self-help-agent to help me think through a recurring frustration.

skills.name: structure-map
skills.summary: Get an overview of a code library: its main parts, how they connect, and where to start.
skills.example: Use $structure-map to show how scikit-learn is organized.

skills.name: student-agent
skills.summary: Check your understanding by teaching a curious student who asks about gaps.
skills.example: Use $student-agent. I will explain database indexes; ask about gaps in my reasoning.

skills.name: tutor-code-file
skills.summary: Understand what a code file does, how it works, and which parts matter.
skills.example: Use $tutor-code-file to explain this file and its important dependencies.

skills.name: tutor-codebase
skills.summary: Learn software engineering by exploring real code, with saved lessons and practice.
skills.example: Use $tutor-codebase to teach the concepts behind this repository.

skills.name: tutor-plain-language
skills.summary: Get a clear explanation of code or text, with small examples you can follow.
skills.example: Use $tutor-plain-language to explain this function with a tiny example.

skills.name: tutor-source-grounded
skills.summary: Study a subject using sources you choose, with a course plan, lessons, and tests.
skills.example: Use $tutor-source-grounded to plan a course on computer networking.

skills.name: tutor-visual
skills.summary: Understand code and systems through diagrams that show how the pieces work together.
skills.example: Use $tutor-visual to show how data moves through this service.
